Job Summary

The UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center’s Office of Community Outreach and Engagement is seeking a mobile mammography program coordinator to expand access to breast cancer screening for underrepresented and medically underserved communities across the Greater Sacramento region. The incumbent will be responsible for providing programmatic, administrative and research implementation support, program evaluation, operational coordination, and patient navigation for the Mobile Mammo+ program. This includes serving as a liaison between the mobile mammography program and collaborating partners to plan; schedule and execute mammography screening days as well as any other future services the mobile clinic offers; manage data collection and reporting for program evaluation; and provide health system navigation and support.

9/4/2026 by 11:59pm

Bachelor's degree in public health or a related field (e.g., health science, nutrition, education, communication, sociology, social science, etc.) and/or the equivalent professional work experience / training.
Experience coordinating health-related programs, community outreach initiatives, research activities, program evaluation efforts, patient navigation services, or comparable projects.
Strong interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across diverse populations.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all co-workers and other stakeholders engaged in the program; to consistently interact with patients and other members of the public with patience, courtesy and professionalism, both in-person and on the telephone; and to effectively respond to individuals who may be angry or upset.
Ability to efficiently use computer system applications for all functions required for this position, including electronic mail, spreadsheets, word processing, REDCap and medical office management, (i.e. scheduling, template maintenance, maintenance of demographic and insurance information).
Ability to learn and navigate the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system (eg. EPIC).
Ability to engage with individuals from diverse cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds effectively.
Proven ability to manage multiple responsibilities, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines.
Ability to accomplish a variety of concurrent assignments in an effective and efficient manner, demonstrating ability to organize, prioritize and complete assignments in a designated time frame.
Ability to adjust to changing workload or assignments and pressures of increased workload or deadlines.
Problem solving skills to independently define a problem identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create viable solutions and take the necessary action to implement problem resolution and ensure prompt and satisfactory resolution.
Decision making skills to independently exercise delegated authority to take action and to appropriately seek assistance from others when limits of delegated authority have been reached.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on patient-centered care and team collaboration.
Ability to apply proper English grammar, spelling and punctuation, sufficient to compose messages and/or routine correspondence, which is clear, concise and easy to understand.
Ability to learn motivational interviewing techniques in order to address and resolve barriers to care effectively.
Typing skills sufficient to use computer keyboard for timely and accurate input and production.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with medically underserved or minority populations in a healthcare setting.
Knowledge of or ability to learn how to use REDCap database.
Knowledge of EPIC (EMR).
Speaks, reads and writes Spanish or another language other than English.
Knowledge of or ability to learn and understand all pertinent laws, regulations, and guidelines governing medical records; confidentiality, privacy, and provision to others, including HIPAA.
Knowledge of or ability to learn about health care insurance systems, which may include Medi-Cal, MediCare, HMO, PPO, fee-for-service, county funded coverage, to support scheduling, follow up care coordination, and billing functions as needed.
Knowledge of proper body mechanics when transferring or assisting patients; ability to safely assist patients.
Ability to handle confidential information such as CD's and other medical documents.

Key Responsibilities

55% - MOBILE MAMMO+ PROGRAM COORDINATOR
40% - MOBILE MAMMO+ DATA COLLECTION, RESEARCH IMPLEMENTATION, PROGRAM EVALUATION AND REPORTING
5% - OTHER AD-HOC DUTIES

Department Overview

The University of California, Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center (UCDCCC) is a Comprehensive Cancer Center designated by the National Cancer Institute, and an Organized Research Unit under the Office of Research. UCDCCC is a clinical and research enterprise consisting of 255 faculty members from the Davis, Sacramento, and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory campuses with research funding totaling $54M. The UCDCCC's Office of Community Outreach and Engagement (COE) catalyzes, conducts, and leads bidirectional outreach and engagement that addresses the cancer control, prevention and research needs of our 19-county catchment area (Alpine, Amador, Butte, Calaveras, Colusa, El Dorado, Glenn, Merced, Nevada, Sacramento, San Joaquin, Solano, Sierra, Stanislaus, Sutter, Tehama, Placer, Yolo, and Yuba).

Department Specific Job Scope

The MobileMammo+ Program Coordinator supports the UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center's Office of Community Outreach and Engagement by coordinating mobile health services designed to improve access to screening, diagnostic, and treatment services for medically underserved populations. The incumbent serves as a liaison among UC Davis Health clinical departments, community organizations, external health systems, and patients to facilitate mobile screening events, patient navigation, data collection, program evaluation, and research activities. The position contributes to outreach, implementation, quality improvement, and reporting efforts that support the Cancer Center's objectives to reduce the cancer burden throughout its 19-county catchment area.

Responsibilities include coordinating outreach and screening events; facilitating patient scheduling, registration, eligibility verification, and follow-up care; supporting community partnerships and stakeholder engagement; maintaining and reporting program and research data; assisting with program evaluation, quality improvement, and grant reporting activities; and providing health system navigation to address barriers to care. The incumbent supports implementation of research and evidence-based interventions designed to improve cancer screening, diagnostic follow-up, and treatment access, while ensuring compliance with institutional, regulatory, clinical, and funding requirements.

The position works collaboratively with clinical, research, operational, and community partners to support the successful delivery, evaluation, and expansion of mobile health services and contributes to the achievement of the Cancer Center's community outreach and engagement goals.

Department Information
Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Do you set high standards for yourself and enjoy a collaborative and challenging work environment? The mission of the California Department of Social Services is to serve, protect, and support the people of California experiencing need in ways that empower wellbeing and disrupt systemic inequities. The vision of the California Department of Social Services is to provide quality services with a commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and equitable California where all people can thrive.

The Research, Automation, and Data Division’s (RADDs) mission is to improve the way the Department collects, manages, and deploys data to support the efficient, effective, and equitable delivery of government social services. RADD manages major statewide initiatives to streamline and automate eligibility determination and benefit administration for key safety net programs, and leads efforts such as human-centered design, data governance, automation and continuous quality improvement, data visualization and analysis, and research partnerships to improve client outcomes and promote program integrity. Across these efforts, RADD provides coaching to the Department on all aspects of the data lifecycle.

CDSS Guiding Principles

Diversity. Equity. Inclusion. Accessibility. Belonging.

Community Engagement

Data Defined Outcomes
We equitably collect and analyze data, take data-driven action, and measure outcomes relevant to those we serve, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Job Description And Duties
Are you ready to champion data that drives real change for California families? Join the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Specialist II, where you’ll transform raw data into accurate, timely data products that influence policy decisions, support budget development, and inform how counties deliver critical services. As part of the Research, Automation & Data Division (RADD), and the Research & Data Insights (RDI) Branch, you will contribute to CDSS’s mission of building a sustainable, data-driven culture. You’ll play a pivotal role in producing accurate data required for State and Federal reporting, supporting program partners, and improving outcomes for vulnerable families statewide.

What You’ll Do

Serve as a technical lead for advanced data engineering, data management, and statistical analysis across major social service programs including child welfare, Temporary Aid for Needy Families (TANF), and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
Build and maintain complex reporting pipelines in Snowflake, extracting, validating, and reconciling data from multiple systems to meet detailed State and Federal reporting requirements. Produce compliant, audit-ready reporting files with robust documentation of methodologies and transformations.
Develop original statistical programming and analytical code using SQL (Snowflake), Python, and R. Design reusable datasets, views, and stored procedures; perform sophisticated joins, window functions, and semi-structured data processing. Produce high-quality insights for program oversight, evaluation, and policy development.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to Research Data Analysts II and Research Data Specialists I, supporting skill development in coding, analytics, and reporting standards. Lead limited-term projects with teams of up to six researchers.

Why Join Us?

Play a key role in building CDSS’s modern, statewide data ecosystem.
Influence high-visibility reporting and analytical work that shapes policy and funding decisions affecting millions.
Collaborate in a mission-driven environment that values innovation, transparency, and human-centered design.
Grow your technical and leadership impact while helping California deliver better services to its most vulnerable populations.

Under the general supervision of the Humanities Administrative Support Center (HASC) Student Affairs Manager, and working closely with the Director of Graduate Studies, the Graduate Program Coordinator is responsible for independently coordinating and managing all aspects of the Graduate Program in the Department of History. 40% GRADUATE ADVISING - Working within Departmental and University guidelines, the Graduate Program Coordinator is the primary source of information about the graduate program for students and faculty. Provides continuous expertise about Graduate Division policies and procedures for faculty, and serves as a liaison between students and faculty regarding all aspects of their academic career. Advises both students and faculty about regulations concerning all graduate matters including registration expectations and deadlines, schedule adjustments, incompletes, withdrawals, leaves of absence, and fellowship eligibility. Monitors every aspect of student progress toward the degree for approximately 100 History graduate students, reviewing grades, counseling students about setting appropriate schedules for meeting requirements and milestones, and exercising personal judgment about calling personal and academic problems to the attention of the Director of Graduate Studies. Maintains and monitors confidential student files, checking that course requirements are fulfilled and that exams are taken at appropriate times. Coordinates all language, comprehensive, and oral qualifying exams with students and faculty, and ensures that appropriate paperwork is completed for the Graduate Division. Participates in policy decisions with the Department Chair and Director of Graduate Studies, providing an informed opinion on university procedures and departmental precedents, as well as relevant information on graduate student status. Uses departmental email lists to keeps students, faculty, alumni, and affiliates informed at all times about relevant deadlines, events, career, and funding opportunities. Demonstrates a strong commitment to the students' personal and academic welfare, creating a climate in which academic and personal problems may be freely discussed, and exercising sound professional judgment in suggesting appropriate courses of action. Maintains close working relationship with Graduate Division and other related offices such as the Office of International Students & Scholars, English for Multilingual Students, Registrar's Office, Billing Office, Career Services, Counseling and Psychological Services, Student Mental Health, Financial Aid, and Cal State University Sacramento for administration of the joint Public History program.
20% GRADUATE PROGRAM ADMINISTRATION - Performs a variety of administrative duties in support of the graduate program. Maintains detailed and up to date reports and records regarding student progress toward degree, faculty dissertation committees, leaves of absence, withdrawals, incompletes, and other changes of status that have implications for student time to degree, graduate student employment, or financial aid. Prepares and maintains confidential correspondence and files regarding student matters. Provides letters of support and verification for past and present graduate students to various external institutions and other departments on campus. Establishes and maintains a database of programmatic and career information of current students and alumni in order to provide detailed individual and statistical data to faculty, staff, and campus administration when requested. Maintains graduate student mailboxes and department directory, and coordinates teaching assistant office assignments. Responsible for the production of graduate program informational material including, but not limited to the Graduate Student Handbook and recruitment brochures. Works closely with CSUS faculty and staff to establish procedures ensuring the smooth operation of the Joint PhD Program on both campuses.
20% GRADUATE ADMISSIONS - Working closely with the Director of Graduate Studies and the faculty admissions committee, oversees the administration of the graduate admissions process. Demonstrates a detailed understanding of the most up to date application policies and procedures as developed and communicated by Graduate Division. Provides accurate and holistic information to prospective students regarding the application process and requirements, program requirements, and financial aid and funding opportunities. Adhering to strict deadlines, uses the Graduate Division's online application portal to review, organize, and ensure completeness of approximately 100 applications per year. Reviews domestic and international student transcripts to verify GPA accuracy and US equivalency. Performs preliminary reading of applications and generates various reports to facilitate the review process. Informs faculty when applications are ready for review, provides online application review portal instructions, and monitors the review process to ensure admissions and fellowship decisions are reached by the posted deadlines. Provides advice to Director of Graduate Studies and admissions committee regarding admissions and fellowship eligibility and creation of support packages, and provides staff support to the committee regarding fellowship allocations and nominations. Prepares and sends departmental acceptance letters, and manages the planning and organization of prospective student recruitment visits. Secures refreshments, meeting rooms, makes hotel reservations, and provides information packets. Coordinates travel reimbursements with Department financial assistant, and manages the recruitment budget as supplied by Graduate Division.

The Department of Biological Sciences focuses on three areas of research and teaching; 1) Cell and Molecular Biology – including biophysics, neuroscience, cell signaling, and developmental biology, and 2) Ecology, Biodiversity – including behavioral ecology, plant-insect interactions, conservation biology, restoration ecology, and evolution and 3) Physiology of Health and Disease including emphasis on human physiology and exercise physiology. new_jobs.description:
POSITION TITLE (Oracle title)

INDIAN EDUCATION PROGRAM COORDINATOR

WORKING TITLE

Indian Education Program Coordinator

SCHOOL/DEPARTMENT

K-12 Academic Enhancement

LOCATION

Crossroads I, Cary, NC

Wake County Public School System (WCPSS) Indian Education Center, Garner, NC

PAY GRADE

Noncertified Grade 28

FLSA STATUS

Nonexempt

ELIGIBILITY FOR EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT

Yes

WORK WEEK SCHEDULE

Monday-Friday (occasional evenings and weekends) Position is available for a hybrid telework workweek

Position Purpose

Organizes, plans, and delivers services to students and families in the WCPSS Indian Education program. Attends monthly parent committee meetings and collaborates with members to ensure compliance with grant objectives. Identifies and supports Native American students in the school system, providing them with support for attendance, social emotional, and academics while encouraging their participation in cultural, educational, and leadership activities in the community. Ensures the program is compliant with WCPSS, state, and federal standards, procedures, and policies. Serves as advocate for American Indian students and as liaison between WCPSS and the larger American Indian community.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES (KSAs)

Considerable knowledge of Microsoft Office, specifically Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point; Google Apps;
Considerable knowledge of PowerSchool;
Knowledge of the needs of students from diverse backgrounds and various learning abilities and styles;
Demonstrated leadership and team building skills;
Excellent organizational skills;
Effective time management skills;
Ability to assess and evaluate program needs and develop short-term and long-term goals and plans;
Ability to prepare and maintain accurate records;
Ability to communicate clearly and concisely both in oral and written form using a variety of communication techniques and tools to ensure the appropriate flow of information, collaborative efforts, and feedback;
Ability to handle and comply with confidentiality policies, security requirements, and testing protocols in a school setting;
Ability to motivate and inspire students;
Ability to monitor the safety and well-being of students;
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with school system staff, staff members of external funding agencies, parents, and the community.

Education, Training, And Experience

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university; AND
Three years of experience of program coordination and delivery of professional development.

An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience which provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully meet the essential duties may be considered.

Certification And License Requirements

Must hold and maintain a valid motor vehicle operator’s license according to the State of North Carolina

requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

A member of a state or federally recognized American Indian tribe.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Organizes, plans, delivers, and documents services to students and parents as outlined by the Title VI Indian Education program grant.
Partners with outside service providers to ensure alignment with WCPSS policies and procedures.
Works closely with principals, teachers, and families to provide services to students; conducts workshops for families and students; works closely with the Indian Education Parent Committee and attends their meetings.
Works to meet the goals and objectives of Indian Education stated in grants; strives to reduce dropout rate, increase enrollment and attendance, and increase the graduation rate of Native American students; tracks student data.
Assists with grant writing and completion of required Indian Education grant documentation.
Conducts home and school visits; assists with finding tutors for students who need them; works with high school seniors in planning their transition to further education, a career, etc.; plans a Career Day and Student Recognition Day for Native American students.
Develops and maintains records of activities, student contacts, etc.; prepares various reports and shares them with the Parent Committee.
Coaches teachers in developing a culturally responsive approach to providing instruction and support to all students.
Makes regular classroom visits to evaluate culturally responsive instructional pedagogy and equitable classroom management with all teachers and staff.
Works with individuals teachers to address specific instructional challenges and to support the development of teacher-student relationships.
Engages in collegial coaching with school administrators and staff to help identify and implement successful equity focused practices leading to closing achievement gaps.
Meets regularly with district leaders to discuss issues related to equity challenges in the schools.
Assists with the overall training support of diversity initiatives and programs and develops strategies for improvement; coordinates the delivery of ongoing and strategic staff development opportunities.
Fosters relationships with established community partners and members of local American Indian tribes.
Organizes/chaperones cultural awareness events, tutoring, camps, and other events for students.
Ensures the program is compliant with WCPSS, state, and federal standards, procedures, and policies.
Performs other duties, as assigned.

WORK ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This job operates in a professional office environment and has a noise level of mostly low to moderate. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and filing cabinets. The position, at times, must be able to come into direct contact with school system staff and staff members of external funding agencies, and the community. Work is considered light physical work, requiring the exertion of up to ten pounds of force. The work frequently requires driving automotive equipment.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
9/2026

They are not intended to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required by the employees assigned to this position. This description may be revised by HR and approved at any time.

Job Details:

General Notes

Established in 2023 as UT Austin’s newest college, the School of Civic Leadership is a community of scholars and students dedicated to studying the foundational ideas and institutions of a free society, with the goal of advancing human flourishing. We value independent thought, civil discourse, reasoned deliberation, and intellectual curiosity as we prepare to meet the challenges of the present and sustain the blessings of liberty for future generations.

Upholding the University’s motto— Disciplina Praesidium Civitatis , “Education is the guardian genius of democracy”—we advance The University of Texas at Austin’s mission to achieve excellence in education, research, and public service.

The University of Texas at Austin provides an outstanding benefits package to staff, including:

Competitive health benefits (Employee premiums covered at 100%; family premiums at 50%)
Vision, dental, life, and disability insurance options
Paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays
Teachers Retirement System of Texas (a defined benefit retirement plan)
Additional voluntary retirement programs: tax sheltered annuity 403(b) and a deferred compensation program 457(b)
Flexible spending account options for medical and childcare expenses
Training and conference opportunities
Tuition assistance
Athletic ticket discounts
Access to UT Austin's libraries and museums
Free rides on all UT Shuttle and Capital Metro buses with staff ID card

Purpose

The Academic Program Coordinator provides administrative support for the School of Civic Leadership's undergraduate academic programs. Reporting to the Associate Director of Academic Affairs, the position maintains academic records, tracks deadlines, prepares routine communications and reports, and supports course scheduling, study abroad, internships, honors theses, assessments, and academic processes.

Responsibilities

Course and Curriculum Support

Collect and enter approved course, instructor, room, and scheduling information; maintain Class Manager, Course Schedule, and related trackers.
Coordinate routine submissions for FaSET, final exams, final grades, catalog updates, room scheduling, and HB 2504 requirements.
Maintain records, distribute approved updates, and flag missing or inconsistent information for review.

Study Abroad and Internship Program Support

Assist in the preparation of materials for program proposals, course scheduling, and student registration. Initiate submission for appropriate approvals.
Maintain timelines, participant records, and routine communications; coordinate approved recruitment information with advisors and communications staff. Assist in the coordination
Maintain applications for internship, assist in the coordination of internship placements and enrollment. Regularly update employers, student, and placement records.
Partner with SCL Career success team to compile and communicate outcome data.

Honors Thesis Support

Update program guides, forms, calendars, and participant records and track student and faculty deadlines.
Coordinate thesis and other related event logistics and collect faculty and student feedback for program review.

Assessment and Reporting

Collect, verify, and organize program data for assessments and recurring reports.
Prepare draft summaries and maintain assessment files and submission records using established templates.

Academic Policy and Appeals Support

Maintain policy resources and confidential appeal records; confirm receipt of required materials and track reviews.
Prepare routine correspondence and refer policy interpretation and decisions to the appropriate administrator or committee.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a related field.
Two years’ experience in related position/field
Demonstrated experience working on projects with multiple stakeholders in a professional setting
Strong interpersonal skills including an interest in supporting student success
Strong organizational skills with ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing summaries, reports, and documentation.
Familiarity with MS Office and Adobe.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience with UT System business policies and procedures.
Demonstrated experience with UT curriculum management systems.
Demonstrated experience coordinating events or projects involving multiple stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to produce and format professional documents, including PDF creation and editing.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with competing deadlines.

Salary Range

$56,000+ depending on qualifications

Required Materials

Resume/CV
3 work references with their contact information; at least one reference should be from a supervisor
Letter of interest

Important

You will be prompted to submit your resume the first time you apply, then you will be provided an option to upload a new Resume for subsequent applications. Any additional Required Materials (letter of interest, references, etc.) will be uploaded in the Application Questions section; you will be able to multi-select additional files.
